title: FOURTH WEST NILE VIRUS POSITIVE
full_story:
Clay County Health Department confirmed the fourth West Nile virus (WNV) positive mosquito sample of the 2026 season in Clay County.  The positive sample was collected in Flora on Friday.  Previously reported WNV positive mosquito batches in Clay County this season included samples collected in Louisville on July 27th, Clay City on August 19th, and Xenia on September 3rd.

Confirmation of WNV positive mosquito samples means that the virus is circulating in the community and there is a heightened risk of infection for humans.  Residents are urged to take the necessary precautions to protect themselves from mosquito bites.  It is important to remember the three R’s – reduce your exposure to mosquitoes, repel them by wearing insect repellant, and report areas where mosquitoes typically breed.

WNV is transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected mosquito.  Mosquitoes pick up the virus by feeding on infected birds.  The illness is not spread from person-to-person.  Most people infected with West Nile virus show no symptoms.  However, some people may experience fever, nausea, headache, and muscle aches.  Symptoms may last from a few days to a few weeks.  In rare cases, severe illness including meningitis or encephalitis, or even death, can occur.  People older than 50 are at higher risk for severe illness from West Nile virus.

Because WNV generally appears and spreads in Illinois mosquito populations as early as two to six weeks before it is transmitted to humans, monitoring the mosquito populations in our communities helps us predict when humans will be at risk for WNV infection.  Surveillance activities in Clay County include laboratory tests on mosquito batches and responding to concerns of mosquito production sites.

If you would like more information on West Nile virus, contact the Clay County Health Department at 662-4406 or visit their website www.healthdept.org.

title: MOSQUITO SPRAYING CONTINUES
full_story:
The City of Flora would like to assure the citizens that the annual spraying for mosquitoes will continue through fall season.  The city began spraying for mosquitoes in early June and will continue through October.  They are currently spraying multiple times a week at dusk throughout the city.

Because grass provides a great cover from the heat of the sun and protection from wind that can blow them away, mosquitoes like to rest in tall grass.  When you don’t mow your lawn, you’re giving mosquitoes a perfect place to hang out and breed.  The shorter the lawn and vegetation, the less opportunity for them to hide out.  Most homeowners like to maintain a nice lawn for aesthetic purposes, but more importantly, you should do it for mosquito prevention.  Luckily, this is an easily avoidable problem.  Here are some tips to make sure your lawn is in check this summer; Mow your lawn often to reduce shade and wind protection provided by tall grass.  Cut back thick vegetation to discourage mosquitoes from nesting.  Clear debris that provide additional cover for mosquitoes such as grass clippings, leaf piles and collections of sticks and branches, and Eliminate Standing Water.  This is where mosquitoes can breed and multiply, making them a never ending problem for homeowners.  Standing water would be considered a pool of freshwater of any size that does not flow.  In order for mosquitoes to breed, they need water; BUT, they don’t need much of it.  They can lay eggs in as little a water bottle cap.

With each generation of mosquito coming every 7 to 10 days, the absolute best way to keep mosquitoes from nesting around your home is the removal of all standing water.  This is the #1 tip in mosquito prevention.  To rid your yard of the most common sources of standing water, be sure to; Check that all gutters around your home are clear and repair any that are broken.  Cover any children’s toys like wagons and sandboxes that could potentially hold water or rainfall.  Overturn any large containers or wheelbarrows in your yard or put them inside a garage or shed.  Remove any birdbaths.  Bring in pet bowls, cups and bottles of water when not in use.  Only bring them out when your pet is going to use them.

title: Louisville Special Meeting
full_story:
Louisville Village trustees made a motion to appoint trustee and former Mayor Chuck Smith as temporary president/mayor of Louisville, releasing Chris Rinehart from his duties as president/mayor for the special village meeting last night.

Village Attorney Kyle Boose explained the state ordinance governing Tax Increment Financing (TIF) prohibits municipal board members who own property within a TIF district from voting on TIF matters or participating in related municipal activities while they own that property.  President/Mayor Chris Rinehart owns property with a storage building and Trustee Scott Ikemire lives in the village’s TIF 2 district.

Both Rinehart and Ikemire left the room during the second meeting.

Trustees then unanimously voted to remove the two properties from the TIF district.

Mayor Rinehart will remain as president of the board with Chuck Smith taking responsibilities in Rinehart’s absence.

title: BUGGY CRASH FOLLOWUP
full_story:
Wayne County Authorities have released the details of a Tuesday morning accident that claimed the life of an Amish teacher and injured 2 children.

Rebecca Esh, 29, a teacher with the Amish community was transporting two students to school in a horse-drawn buggy Tuesday when it was struck from behind by an SUV at about 7:50 am.  The location was west of Johnsonville on Wayne County Highway 16 at County Road 615 E.  Esh was pronounced dead at the scene by Wayne County Coroner Shari Winter.  The two children in the buggy received major injuries and were airlifted from the scene to a trauma center in Evansville.  Their ages, names and condition have not been released.  The driver of the Chevrolet SUV that struck the buggy has been identified only as a 21-year-old woman.  Illinois State Police have not released her name.  She was not injured.  The horse pulling the buggy was seriously injured and had to be put down.

title: COMPUTERS FOR BEGINNERS CLASSES
full_story:
Frontier Community College will offer two Computers for Beginners classes in October for individuals interested in developing their basic computer skills and becoming more comfortable using technology.

The first class will be held on Tuesday from 11:30 am to 4:30 pm, followed by a second opportunity on October 22nd from noon to 4 pm.  Both classes will take place in Room 32 of Workforce Development Center on Frontier Community College’s campus.

Computers for Beginners is designed to provide participants with an opportunity to develop their computer skills in an accessible learning environment.  Whether participants have limited experience with computers or simply want to become more confident with technology, the classes provide an opportunity to strengthen their knowledge and skills.

Those interested in attending can register by contacting KaRissa Miller at 618-847-9276 or by email at [email protected].  Interested people can also register by scanning the QR code on flyers or on the college Facebook page.

title: TROUT FISHING OPENS
full_story:
The 2026 Illinois fall trout fishing season will open on Saturday, October 17th at 60 ponds, lakes and streams throughout the state.

An early catch-and-release trout fishing will open at select sites on Saturday.  No trout may be kept during the catch-and-release period.  Anglers may begin keeping trout when the regular season opens at 5 am October 17th.

In our area trout fishing can be done at Sam Dale Conservation Area Turkey Run Pond in Wayne County.  At the Boston Pond, in the Stephen A. Forbes State Recreation Area in Marion County, and at the Mount Vernon City Park Pond in Jefferson County.

The Illinois Catchable Trout Program is funded through the sale of inland trout stamps.  The Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) stocks more than 80,000 rainbow trout each year at waters where trout fishing is permitted during the fall season.  An additional 80,000 trout are stocked for the spring season, which begins in April.

For the 2026 fall trout season, no trout may be taken from any stocked site before the season opens.  During the season, the daily catch limit is five trout.  All anglers must have a valid Illinois fishing license and inland trout stamp.  Check the IDNR agent locator website for locations. Fishing licenses and trout stamps are also available online.

Anglers should contact individual trout-stocked sites for information about site-specific regulations and opening times.  Not all sites open at 5 am on opening day.  Anglers are encouraged to check the opening time for their preferred fishing location before October 17th.

The fall trout season offers opportunities for families to get outdoors and enjoy fishing.  Resources are available for taking kids fishing online.  For more information on trout seasons and other Illinois fishing opportunities, visit www.ifishillinois.org.

title: TO ELECT 3 NEW MEMBERS
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Agriculture (IDOA) announced an election will be held on October 28th, for two board members in the following Illinois Wheat Development Board Districts (IWDB) three and six as well as one (1) statewide At-Large Board Member.  District six includes Clay, Wayne, Alexander, Edwards, Gallatin, Hamilton, Hardin, Johnson, Massac, Pope, Pulaski, Saline, Union, Wabash, White, Williamson Counties.  As no formal petitions were filed for these vacant board positions, producers of Illinois wheat residing in these Districts may participate in the October 28th, election as a write-in candidate.  Producers must be of legal voting age, reside in the district for which they are running and be a qualified producer of wheat.  At-large write-in candidates may reside in any of the IWDB Districts.

Absentee ballots are available to those not available to vote in person by contacting IDOA at 217-524-1083 or by email at agr.marketnews.illinois.gov.  In-person voting will take place at the county Farm Bureau offices in Illinois during normal business hours.

For more information, call IDOA at (217) 524-1083 or the Illinois Wheat Association at (309) 557-3619.

title: ANDHEALTH TODAY EXPANDS
full_story:
AndHealth today announced its expansion into Illinois through a partnership with the Illinois Primary Health Care Association (IPHCA) and its first Illinois community health center partner, Christopher Rural Health Planning Corporation.  The announcement was made at IPHCA’s annual conference in Peoria.

Through the partnership, patients of Christopher Rural Health Planning Corporation will gain access to Whole Person Specialty Care across rheumatology, dermatology, and neurology, through AndHealth’s own specialist team and a growing network of partnered specialty practices in the region, with dramatically shorter wait times than they face today.  Patients will also receive comprehensive disease management support, including care navigation, health coaching, nutritional support, and help with prior authorizations and scheduling, all connected to the primary care team they already know and trust.  Over the coming year, the partnership will also expand specialty pharmacy access for Christopher Rural Health Planning Corporation patients.
